title: Alex West on CyberLeads' decline: S curves, business genetics, and Shotgun to Sniper
summary: Alex West recounts burning out as CyberLeads declined from about $500k/year, pivoting to a $3k consulting offer, and spending a year writing his books. He distills what he learned: businesses are sequences of S curves that eventually fall, waves shape outcomes more than models, and growth comes from shotgunning products, sniping a winner, then shotgunning again for the next lever.

principles.text: Businesses are a sequence of S curves, each with its own plateau, and each eventually rises, plateaus and falls.
principles.quote: Businesses are a sequence of S curves, each one reaching a different plateau.

principles.text: Price is the easiest growth lever; new channels are hardest, retention via product is in between.
principles.quote: Building new channels is the hardest. And making people pay more is by far the easiest and most effective lever to pull.

principles.text: Find the distribution channel and market first, then the idea. Building a unique product first never worked for him.
principles.quote: What worked, and the way I found CyberLeads, was thinking of my distribution channel and market first, because those are the hardest to build in the current business environment, and then the actual idea.

principles.text: Shotgun many products until one works, then sniper on it until the plateau, then shotgun again for the next growth lever.
principles.quote: Shotgun many products until you find a successful one

principles.text: Success often comes from the business's genetics (channel, pricing, timing, brand), so don't mistake it for personal mastery.
principles.quote: I mistook my success for mastery.

principles.text: Entrepreneurship is choosing which waves to ride, adapt to, or ignore. Ignoring all waves forever is the wrong lesson.
principles.quote: I think the magic of entrepreneurship is deciding how to respond to each wave while sailing the oceans. Which waves to capitalize on. Which waves to adapt to. And which waves to completely ignore.
